handoff: Status: exploration done, no game files changed. Answer: nothing has to be downloaded. details.note:
VDB EXPLORATION (T31). Verified = ran on local Godot 4.7.2 / shell. Unverified = my knowledge.
a) OpenVDB (.vdb): sparse hierarchical voxel container from DreamWorks, used by Houdini/Blender for smoke and clouds. [unverified, knowledge]
 Godot has no VDB support. VERIFIED by headless ClassDB query: no class with 'VDB' in the name (OpenVDB/VDB: false); recognized Texture3D extensions are only tres, res, dds. No importer.
 VERIFIED present: FogVolume, FogMaterial, Texture3D, ImageTexture3D (create() with 8x8x8 R8 returned OK), NoiseTexture3D, CompressedTexture3D, Texture3DRD, VoxelGI, GPUParticles3D, MultiMeshInstance3D; fog shaders with sampler3D compile in the class list check (shader_type fog; not compiled on GPU headless).
b) Default-tool replacements (costs are guesses, no rendering possible here):
 1 Baked grid as ImageTexture3D (e.g. 64x64x16 R8, ~64 KB; our own GDScript bake, or a .tres/.res/.dds). Needs: bake script only. Render via FogVolume + shader_type fog (needs Environment volumetric fog on; it is a froxel pass, a guess: 1-3 ms on Apple GPU, hardware-dependent) or a raymarch spatial shader on a box (guess 1-4 ms, cost scales with steps x screen area). Quality: real dust lanes and sun glow. Risk: untested visually, Compatibility renderer lacks fog volumes (UNKNOWN which renderer the project uses at export).
 2 Layered billboard sprites: 8-20 alpha quads of baked dust slices. Needs: slice images from the bake. Guess <0.5 ms. Quality: ok from top-down, banding if camera tilts. Risk: low.
 3 Star point cloud with density-driven tint (what star_field.gd already is, plus a per-star light value baked from the grid). Guess ~0.1 ms for 3000-20000 quads. Quality: dust shows as dark gaps and tinted stars, no smooth glow. Risk: lowest.
 Light propagation (sun to grid) is a one-time CPU bake in GDScript (64x64x16 = 65k cells, a few suns: well under a second, guess). It is needed in every option and does not use VDB.
c) Installed (VERIFIED by commands): python3 3.9.6, numpy NOT installed, openvdb python module NOT installed, 'which blender' empty but /Applications/Blender.app exists and runs (5.1), Houdini 22.0.466 is installed (/Applications/Houdini). Both can author and export .vdb. Nothing needs downloading for options 1-3 because the bake can be pure GDScript (or plain Python without numpy). A .vdb would only be needed if the owner wants to author clouds by hand in Blender/Houdini; then a converter VDB -> raw 3D grid is required (Blender or Houdini scripting can write raw slices/PNG stacks; not tested). Not checked: whether Blender/Houdini licences or scripting work in this sandbox.
d) Recommendation: skip VDB. Bake our own grid in GDScript (we only need low-res).
 Step 1 (S): bake density grid from the existing point cloud + sun propagation in GDScript, store per-star light, tint stars. Gives option 3 immediately.
 Step 2 (M): store grid as ImageTexture3D, add a cheap look: either 12-16 billboard dust slices (option 2) or FogVolume (option 1).
 Step 3 (S): owner screenshot check on macOS and frame time measurement; pick FogVolume vs slices from the result.
 Owner decides: (1) does he need hand-authored clouds in Blender/Houdini (then VDB-to-grid export is extra work, size M), or is a procedural galaxy fine; (2) quality target: dark dust gaps only (option 3) or visible glowing volume (option 1); (3) which renderer is used for the macOS export (Forward+/Mobile vs Compatibility).
 Could not settle here: real frame cost and look of FogVolume/raymarch on macOS; needs a rendered run on the owner's machine.
